text:
Jamal: Quick profiling dump from this morning's sweep. Tested channels=1/4/8, proto=LL vs LL128, algo variants (ring/tree). Attached summary below — all-reduce drops a lot but E2E step latency isn't uniformly better. TL;DR: comm wins, but KV/cache + kernel scheduling are fighting overlap.

Jamal: Summary (4xA100, 8k seq, batch=2):
- baseline (1 ch, default): all-reduce ~10.8 ms, step ~198 ms
- 4 ch, proto=LL: all-reduce ~6.2 ms (-43%), step ~187 ms (-5.6%)
- 8 ch, proto=LL128: all-reduce ~5.9 ms (-45%), step ~182 ms (-8.1%)
- 4 ch + LL threshold tuning: all-reduce ~5.1 ms, step ~176 ms (-11.2%)
Notes: KV cache miss events cause ~12-20 ms stalls on some micro-batches, which reduces the end-to-end wins.

Maria: Nice. Can you paste the exact env + how you group TP/PP? Which runtime commit?

Jamal: Run command we used:
```
NCCL_ALGO=8 NCCL_PROTO=LL128 NCCL_NSOCKS_PERTHREAD=8 \nNCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=^lo,docker0 NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=GROUP \npython -m perf.run --model=3b --tp-groups=2 --channels=8 --prefetch=0
```
Pinned to commit 9d3f7a2 (runtime: kernel selection tweaks + kv barrier).

Lee: Where are you seeing the KV misses? GPU timeline (nsys) or host logs?

Jamal: nsys timeline: compute -> all-reduce -> KV lookup -> stall (waiting on memcpy) -> compute. The problem is that KV memcpy is happening on the same stream after the all-reduce, so we lose overlap.

PerfBot: perfbot: job=1752-sweep finished. Quick alert: +3% median latency regression on 3B small-batch (batch=1/2) for LL128+8ch vs baseline. See /perf/jobs/1752.

Alex: A few quick ideas: try NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=GROUP vs PARALLEL (GROUP can reduce kernel launch overhead). Also try lowering NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD or NCCL_LL128_THRESHOLD to force different lanes.

Maria: Could this be the runtime change that selected the int8 matmul kernel by default? I vaguely recall that added a sync point to flush the KV state.

Lee: Yeah commit 9d3f7a2 added a barrier after kernel selection for safety (comment: "ensure KV view consistent"). That barrier will kill overlap.

Jamal: Confirmed. On a branch where I revert just that barrier, we recover ~6-7 ms of step latency in the LL128/8ch config. But KV correctness tests fail intermittently — need to prefetch earlier.

Alex: Also try NCCL_BUFFER_SIZE tuning and NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME set appropriately. For LL128 specifically, NCCL_NSOCKS_PERTHREAD=8 + bigger buffer helped for us.

Maria: Any chance kernel scheduling (streams/priority) is causing serialization? We used to put all-reduce on a low-priority stream to allow memcpy to run concurrently.

Jamal: Current placement: compute=default stream, all-reduce=high-priority comm stream, KV memcpy=default (blocked). I want to move KV memcpy to low-priority async stream and bump compute to highest. Will try tonight.

Lee: Also add an instrumented nsys capture with these envs: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL and include timeline markers in runtime for: KERNEL_SELECT_START/END, ALLREDUCE_START/END, KV_COPY_START/END. That'll make it obvious.

PerfBot: perfbot: created issue perf/1752 with attached traces.

Alex: FYI: in prior runs we saw that GROUP launch reduced CPU-side enqueue cost but increased GPU kernel queueing in weird ways when channel count >4. So there's a tradeoff: CPU overhead vs kernel interleaving.

Maria: Sounds like plan: Jamal runs focused sweep with (1) revert barrier, (2) KV prefetch async stream, (3) NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=GROUP, (4) try channels=4 and 8 with LL128, and (5) include nsys + timeline markers. Please post the small CSV results here. :eyes:

Jamal: Will run overnight and post CSV + traces tomorrow. If the revert breaks correctness, I'll instead implement prefetch + reorder to keep barrier out of critical path. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Alex: Ping me if you want me to run the same on the 80GB nodes. Could be different due to PCIe vs NVLink.

Maria: thx — tag me when done, I want to update the perf dashboard.

PerfBot: perfbot: reaction :white_check_mark:
